title: Central Bureau of Investigation v. B. Ramalinga Raju & Ors. (Satyam Corporate Fraud)
crime_type: Corporate Accounting Fraud / Insider Trading / Falsification of Accounts
court_or_authority: Special CBI Sessions Court, Hyderabad / High Court of Telangana
legal_citation: Special CC No. 1/2010 (CBI Court Hyderabad); (2015) CriLJ 3120
source: CBI Special Court Hyderabad & Indian Kanoon (doc/79261053)
ipc_sections: Section 468 IPC (Forgery for purpose of cheating)
Section 471 IPC (Using forged document as genuine)
evidence: Over 7,500 fabricated client invoices generated under hidden IP addresses showing fictitious software services revenue
Forged fixed-deposit bank confirmation letters purportedly from BNP Paribas, HDFC Bank, and Citibank totaling over ₹5,000 crore
Written confession letter submitted by Ramalinga Raju to company board and market regulators on January 7, 2009
Audit discrepancies exposed by SFIO and CBI forensic digital accounting tools
modus_operandi: Systematically inflated revenue and operating profits over a decade by injecting thousands of fictitious client invoices into the ERP system. Created fake bank accounts and fabricated fixed deposit receipts to mirror the non-existent cash reserves on balance sheets, using artificially high share prices to pledge shares for real estate investments.
personality_disorder: High-functioning white-collar deceit, compulsive prestige preservation, and catastrophic escalation of commitment.
common_traits: Fictitious invoice generation in corporate ERP
Balance sheet inflation to preserve stock valuation
Diversion of corporate funds to family real estate entities
summary: Often described as India Enron, the Satyam scam saw ₹7,000+ crore inflated on company books. CBI Special Court convicted founder B. Ramalinga Raju and nine others in 2015 to rigorous imprisonment and fines.
